title: New DARCYS Awards Celebrate Disability Stories in Movies and TV
summary:
On Saturday, Easterseals held the first Disability Arts & Culture Awards, called The DARCYs, in Santa Monica, California. The awards honor movies and shows that include people with disabilities in true-to-life ways.

Coverage said winners included the drama "The Pitt" and the film "Take Me Home." The published list also named "Horsegirls" as Best Feature and "The Haunting of Pennhurst" as Best Documentary. Most judges on the committees are people with disabilities.

Tina Frim hosted the night. Geri Jewell received a Legacy Award, and Vincent Rutley received an emerging talent award. Singer Lachi performed. Easterseals Southern California and Film Independent put on the event.

Leaders said the awards continue a tradition that began in 1979 and thank storytellers who change how disability is seen. For kids who love film and TV, it shows that inclusive stories are celebrated as excellent entertainment.
